entries.ex: Rising incomes mean that people now spend more money on *leisure* than ever before.
entries.exAr: يعني ارتفاع الدخل أن الناس ينفقون اليوم على *أنشطة أوقات الفراغ* أكثر من أي وقت مضى.

entries.ex: Taking up a creative *hobby* such as painting can help reduce stress after work.
entries.exAr: قد تساعد ممارسة *هواية* إبداعية مثل الرسم على تخفيف التوتر بعد العمل.

entries.ex: Gardening has long been a favourite *pastime* for retired people in Britain.
entries.exAr: لطالما كانت البستنة *تسلية* مفضلة لدى المتقاعدين في بريطانيا.

entries.ex: The council has turned the old factory site into a park for public *recreation*.
entries.exAr: حولت البلدية موقع المصنع القديم إلى حديقة عامة *للاستجمام*.

entries.ex: Regular swimming is an excellent way to improve overall *fitness* without straining the joints.
entries.exAr: تعد السباحة المنتظمة وسيلة ممتازة لتحسين *اللياقة البدنية* عمومًا دون إجهاد المفاصل.

entries.ex: Professional *athletes* often train for several hours every day.
entries.exAr: يتدرب *الرياضيون* المحترفون عادة عدة ساعات يوميًا.

entries.ex: Some parents worry that *competitive* sport puts too much pressure on young children.
entries.exAr: يخشى بعض الآباء أن تضع الرياضة *التنافسية* ضغطًا كبيرًا على الأطفال الصغار.

entries.ex: The country spent billions preparing stadiums to host the international *tournament*.
entries.exAr: أنفقت الدولة المليارات على تجهيز الملاعب لاستضافة *البطولة* الدولية.

entries.ex: More than 80,000 *spectators* filled the stadium for the final.
entries.exAr: ملأ أكثر من ثمانين ألف *متفرج* الملعب لمشاهدة المباراة النهائية.

entries.ex: Many *amateur* clubs depend entirely on volunteers to survive.
entries.exAr: يعتمد كثير من *أندية الهواة* اعتمادًا كاملًا على المتطوعين للاستمرار.

entries.ex: Group sports at school help children develop *team spirit* and cooperation.
entries.exAr: تساعد الرياضات الجماعية في المدرسة الأطفال على تنمية *روح الفريق* والتعاون.

entries.ex: The WHO recommends that adults do at least 150 minutes of moderate *physical activity* a week.
entries.exAr: توصي منظمة الصحة العالمية بأن يمارس البالغون ما لا يقل عن 150 دقيقة من *النشاط البدني* المعتدل أسبوعيًا.

entries.ex: Many office workers go to the *gym* before work to stay in shape.
entries.exAr: يذهب كثير من موظفي المكاتب إلى *الصالة الرياضية* قبل العمل للحفاظ على لياقتهم.

entries.ex: Schools should give pupils more time for *outdoor activities* such as hiking and camping.
entries.exAr: ينبغي أن تمنح المدارس التلاميذ وقتًا أطول لممارسة *الأنشطة في الهواء الطلق* مثل المشي الطويل والتخييم.

entries.ex: Doctors link many modern illnesses to an unhealthy *lifestyle*.
entries.exAr: يعزو الأطباء كثيرًا من الأمراض الحديثة إلى *نمط الحياة* غير الصحي.

entries.ex: A short, intense *workout* can be as effective as a long run.
entries.exAr: قد يكون *التمرين* القصير المكثف فعالًا بقدر الجري لمسافة طويلة.

entries.ex: Marathon runners need great *stamina* to keep going for over 42 kilometres.
entries.exAr: يحتاج عداؤو الماراثون إلى *قدرة كبيرة على التحمل* لمواصلة الجري مسافة تزيد على 42 كيلومترًا.

entries.ex: Warming up properly before exercise reduces the risk of *injury*.
entries.exAr: يقلل الإحماء الجيد قبل التمرين من خطر *الإصابة*.

entries.ex: A good *coach* motivates players as well as teaching them technical skills.
entries.exAr: *المدرب* الجيد يحفز اللاعبين إلى جانب تعليمهم المهارات الفنية.

entries.ex: Video technology now helps the *referee* make fairer decisions during matches.
entries.exAr: تساعد تقنية الفيديو اليوم *الحكم* على اتخاذ قرارات أكثر عدلًا خلال المباريات.

entries.ex: She won her first world *championship* at the age of just nineteen.
entries.exAr: أحرزت أول *بطولة* عالمية لها وهي في التاسعة عشرة من عمرها فقط.

entries.ex: *Extreme sports* like skydiving attract people who enjoy taking risks.
entries.exAr: تجذب *الرياضات الخطرة* مثل القفز المظلي الأشخاص الذين يستمتعون بالمخاطرة.

entries.ex: For many families, television is still the main source of *entertainment* in the evening.
entries.exAr: لا يزال التلفاز مصدر *الترفيه* الرئيسي لدى كثير من الأسر في المساء.

entries.ex: Deep breathing and gentle stretching are popular methods of *relaxation*.
entries.exAr: يعد التنفس العميق والتمدد الخفيف من طرق *الاسترخاء* الشائعة.

entries.ex: Long working hours can leave young professionals with very little *social life*.
entries.exAr: قد تترك ساعات العمل الطويلة للمهنيين الشباب *حياة اجتماعية* محدودة جدًا.

entries.ex: Video games are sometimes blamed for turning teenagers into *couch potatoes*.
entries.exAr: تُلام ألعاب الفيديو أحيانًا على تحويل المراهقين إلى *كسالى ملازمين للأرائك*.

entries.ex: Shaking hands with your opponent after a match is a sign of good *sportsmanship*.
entries.exAr: تعد مصافحة الخصم بعد المباراة علامة على *الروح الرياضية* العالية.

entries.ex: Several cyclists were banned after testing positive for *performance-enhancing drugs*.
entries.exAr: مُنع عدد من الدراجين من المنافسة بعد ثبوت تعاطيهم *المنشطات*.

entries.ex: In hot countries, *indoor* sports centres allow people to exercise all year round.
entries.exAr: في البلدان الحارة، تتيح المراكز الرياضية *المغلقة* للناس ممارسة الرياضة طوال العام.

entries.ex: Many students spend their *spare time* volunteering in their local community.
entries.exAr: يقضي كثير من الطلاب *وقت فراغهم* في العمل التطوعي في مجتمعهم المحلي.

gap.s: A serious knee ____ forced him to miss the rest of the season.
Tickets sold out quickly, and over 60,000 ____ watched the match live.
My morning ____ usually includes twenty minutes of running and some weights.
The ____ sent off two players for dangerous tackles in the first half.
Unlike professionals, ____ players are not paid for taking part in competitions.
After months of training, she finally had the ____ to complete a full marathon.
Twenty-four teams will take part in this year's ____, which starts next month.
Congratulating the winning team showed real ____ from the young players.

para.a: I like to play football when I am not working.
para.b: Football is my favourite *pastime* when I am not at work.

para.a: People today sit a lot and do not move much.
para.b: Many people today lead a sedentary *lifestyle* with little exercise.

para.a: He can run for a long time without getting tired.
para.b: He has remarkable *stamina* and rarely tires, even on long runs.

para.a: Many people enjoy dangerous sports like rock climbing.
para.b: *Extreme sports* such as rock climbing are increasingly popular.

p1.q: What do you usually do in your spare time?
p1.a: In my *spare time*, I usually go to the *gym* three or four times a week, because it helps me stay focused at work. At weekends I prefer something more relaxing, like reading or meeting friends at a café.

p1.q: Did you play any sports when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, I played football almost every day with the boys in my neighbourhood. We weren't very skilled, but it taught me a lot about *team spirit*, and I think that's why I still enjoy group activities today.

p1.q: Do you prefer indoor or outdoor activities?
p1.a: It depends on the season. In summer it's far too hot where I live, so I tend to choose *indoor* options like swimming. But in winter I love *outdoor activities*, especially camping in the desert with my family.

p2.cue: Describe a sport or physical activity you enjoy doing.
points: when and where you do it
and explain why you enjoy it
p2.a: I'd like to talk about swimming, which has been my favourite form of *physical activity* since I was about ten. I usually swim at an *indoor* pool near my office, three evenings a week after work, and on Fridays I sometimes go to the beach with my brothers. Most of the time I swim alone, but I occasionally join a small group of *amateur* swimmers who train together, and we have a *coach* who gives us advice on technique. There are several reasons why I enjoy it so much. Firstly, it is excellent for overall *fitness*, and it has really improved my *stamina*; a few years ago I could barely swim four lengths, whereas now I can manage forty without stopping. Secondly, unlike running, it is gentle on the joints, so the risk of *injury* is quite low. But above all, it is a great form of *relaxation*. When I am in the water, I forget about work completely, and I always feel calmer afterwards.

p3.q: Why do some people prefer watching sport to playing it?
p3.a: I think there are a few reasons. For some, watching is simply a form of *entertainment*, much like going to the cinema. Others may lack the time or *fitness* to play regularly. Also, being a *spectator* at a big match creates a sense of belonging, because you share the excitement with thousands of other fans. Of course, the risk is that people become *couch potatoes* who only watch and never move.

p3.q: Should professional athletes who are caught using drugs be banned from sport for life?
p3.a: That's a tough one. On the one hand, *performance-enhancing drugs* are a form of cheating, and they go against the whole idea of *sportsmanship*, so strict punishment is necessary. On the other hand, a lifetime ban might be too harsh for a first offence, especially for young *athletes* who were badly advised. Personally, I'd support a long ban first and a lifetime ban for anyone who does it again.

writing.q: In many countries, people are becoming less physically active, and levels of obesity are rising. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: In recent decades, many societies have seen a sharp decline in *physical activity*, accompanied by a worrying rise in obesity. This essay will examine the main causes of this trend and suggest several measures that individuals, schools and governments could take to reverse it.

The most obvious cause is the modern *lifestyle*. Many adults now work in offices, where they sit at a desk for eight hours a day, and then drive home rather than walk. In their *spare time*, people increasingly turn to screen-based *entertainment* such as streaming services and video games instead of *outdoor activities*. Children are particularly affected: in many cities there are few safe places to play, so they spend their evenings indoors. As a result, an entire generation risks becoming *couch potatoes* who rarely break a sweat.

Nevertheless, there are practical solutions. Firstly, schools should guarantee at least one hour of sport every day and encourage *competitive* as well as non-competitive games, so that every child finds something they enjoy. Secondly, local authorities could invest in parks, cycle lanes and affordable *recreation* centres, making exercise part of daily life. Finally, employers might offer subsidised *gym* membership or flexible hours, which would make it easier for busy workers to fit a *workout* into their routine.

In conclusion, inactivity is largely the result of sedentary jobs and screen-based *leisure*, as well as a lack of safe public spaces. However, if schools, councils and employers work together to make exercise easy, enjoyable and affordable, it should be possible to build a fitter and healthier society.
